text: dsh-skill-mcp-tool 是一款面向 DSH Web 客户端的 Skills 与 MCP 管理插件，在设置页和主界面侧栏提供统一面板，并通过宿主路由管理本机技能文件和 MCP 配置。它可浏览、创建、编辑、启停技能，从 Git 安装或更新技能，管理 MCP 服务器与 OAuth 授权，并导入导出备份。适合需要集中维护技能和 MCP 连接的 DSH 用户。需要本机 Git 执行仓库操作；不要求插件专属 API Key。

dsh-skill-mcp-tool manages Skills and MCP servers in the DSH web client. Its settings and sidebar panel lets users edit skills, install them from Git, manage MCP configurations and OAuth, and move backups. It requires local Git for repository operations and no plugin-specific API key.
想在一个面板里统一管理 DSH 的技能和 MCP 服务器。
怎么从 Git 仓库安装或更新 DSH skill？
我希望在 DSH 里启用和停用本地技能。
能不能编辑技能说明并检查 frontmatter 格式？
想给 DSH 添加需要 OAuth 登录的 MCP 服务。
如何把技能和 MCP 配置备份后迁移到另一台机器？
I want to manage my DSH skills and MCP servers in one panel.
How can I install or update a skill from a Git repository?
dsh-skill-mcp-tool 的功能「Git 安装技能」：从 Git 仓库发现并安装有效技能，也可再次拉取更新；用户在面板提供仓库来源并选择目标技能根目录。
dsh-skill-mcp-tool 的功能「技能管理」：列出技能并支持创建、编辑、删除和启停；停用通过重命名技能文件实现，provider 刷新后即可反映变化。
dsh-skill-mcp-tool 的功能「MCP 管理」：在面板增删改 MCP 服务器配置并切换启用状态，配置写入受管的 profile cordis.patch.yml 区块。
dsh-skill-mcp-tool 的功能「MCP OAuth 授权」：为支持的 HTTP MCP 服务器启动授权、刷新或断开流程，并把访问令牌关联到服务器配置。
dsh-skill-mcp-tool 的功能「设置备份迁移」：将技能、MCP 配置和来源记录打包；导入前生成计划，用户确认后再应用变更。
dsh-skill-mcp-tool 使用前须知：Git 安装和更新依赖本机 Git；MCP OAuth 回调会在本机 127.0.0.1 随机端口监听。
dsh-skill-mcp-tool 使用前须知：OAuth 刷新令牌存于本机 oauth.json，访问令牌会写入 profile 的 MCP 配置；备份是否包含 MCP 密钥由导出选项决定。

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that puts **Skills and MCP servers under one roof**, reachable from both the settings menu and a main-interface sidebar entry — with **hot-reload enable/disable toggles** and **Git-based skill install/update**.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：**Two entry points, one panel**

- Settings menu → "技能与 MCP" / "Skills & MCP" page.
- Main interface → a sidebar icon row that opens the same panel in the centre column.

Both render the identical component, so the four tabs (Skills / MCP / Remote sources / Backup) behave the same wherever you open them.

**The plugin updates itself from the panel**

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：A **version card** sits above the tab strip, styled exactly like the proxy card next to it: it shows the running version, checks the upstream repository on demand, and offers a one-click update when a newer tag — or newer commits on the default branch — exist.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：- **Check** compares the installed version and the commit recorded in `pnpm-lock.yaml` against `git ls-remote` of the repository declared in `package.json`, using the same proxy as skill installs. It reports a version bump, a newer commit without a tag, "up to date", or "local-dir install, not checked".
- **Update** runs `pnpm add <the spec your profile already records>` in a **detached child process** — it does not uninstall the plugin. If it fails, the running version keeps working; on success you restart DSH to load the new code.
- It never occupies the request: the panel polls a status file, so a 30-second install does not hang the page, and the outcome survives a closed panel.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：> **Why not hot-swap?** The host half is ESM cached by URL and the client bundle is cached by the browser, so an in-place replacement cannot take effect without a restart anyway. The panel says so instead of claiming success.

**Layout: the two entry points are handled separately**

The host's layout contract differs between the centre panel and the settings page, so the shell has two modes selected by `data-surface`:

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：- **Centre panel (opened from the sidebar icon)**: the host supplies neither padding nor a scroll container, so the plugin provides both — centred content with breathing room (up to 48px per side, shrinking responsively on narrow windows) plus its own scrolling.
- **Settings page**: the host already renders the section inside its content column (padding and scrolling included), so the plugin adds nothing on top — no doubled inset, no nested scrollbars.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：**Scrolling: long skill lists stay reachable, with no visible scrollbar**

In the centre panel only the list scrolls while **the title and tabs stay pinned to the top**, so the refresh button and tab strip remain reachable even at the bottom of a long list, with breathing room after the last row.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：**No visible scrollbar at all**: the wheel, trackpad, touch, and keyboard (arrow keys / PageUp / PageDown) all keep working — only the bar is no longer drawn. The horizontal insets therefore *always* equal the inner padding: symmetric left and right regardless of content length or whether scrolling is needed, with no sideways jump when a scrollbar would have appeared or disappeared. The same rules cover modals, so long forms still scroll.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：`scrollbar-gutter: stable` is deliberately *not* used: it reserves scrollbar width even when the content fits (measured: `stable` 15px, `stable both-edges` 30px), leaving an empty band on a page that has nothing to scroll. All three hiding mechanisms are declared — `scrollbar-width`, `-ms-overflow-style`, and `::-webkit-scrollbar` — so no browser falls back to a native bar that would skew the insets.

**Ordering: alphabetical, always**

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：- **Skills**: grouped by source, with a fixed group order of **project → user → plugin → other** (it does not shift as skills come and go, so group headings stay put); **alphabetical by name within each group**.
- **MCP servers**: managed and external rows are each sorted alphabetically by server name.
- **Remote sources**: sorted alphabetically by repository label.
- Sorting is **case-insensitive**: `Chrome_DevTools_MCP` sorts before `REA`, instead of all uppercase names clumping at the top. Only when two names are identical in lowercase does the raw string break the tie, keeping the order stable.
- Managed rows are written to `cordis.patch.yml` in that same order, so the file and the UI never disagree.
- Ordering is applied at the single choke point every write path goes through, so add/edit/enable/disable/delete can't bypass it.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：- Lists every skill from all four standard roots, in official rank order: project `.dsh/skills` (100) → project `.agents/skills` (200) → user `~/.dsh/skills` (400) → user `~/.agents/skills` (500).
- Handles both layouts: directory bundles (`<name>/SKILL.md`) and flat files (`<name>.md`), plus nested/categorised trees.
- **Enable/disable is a lossless rename**: `SKILL.md` ⇄ `SKILL.md.disabled` (or `<name>.md` ⇄ `<name>.md.disabled`). The official provider only recognises the exact filenames, so the skill leaves the catalog while its files and `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` stay fully intact. The provider's watcher picks the change up on the next catalog refresh — **no restart**.
- Malformed skills stay listed but flagged **格式不合规 / Invalid format**, so you can fix or delete them rather than being unable to see them.
- Plugin-registered skills (no file on disk) are listed read-only.
- Create, edit, and delete skills through the built-in editor; frontmatter is validated before anything touches disk.
- **Install / update from Git**: shallow-clone a repository (or a subdirectory of one), discover every valid skill inside, and copy it to the chos

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：> Why this plugin supplies its own provider: the host-level `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` row is deliberately disabled by the web app (its comment reads “presets own local discovery”), leaving each agent preset to mount its own. On some presets that provider does not actually take effect — skills on disk then appear neither in `/` nor to the model. This plugin does not depend on the preset being correct; it registers the roots it manages itself.

**Proxy: a Git proxy field above the tabs**

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：On many networks a direct `git clone` of a repository times out, which makes installing and updating skills impossible. A **proxy bar sits above the four tabs** — it is a prerequisite shared by every Git operation in every tab (install, update, check for updates), not a setting belonging to one of them.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：- **Command-scoped, never global.** The address is injected as `git -c http.proxy=… -c https.proxy=… <subcommand>`. **Your global git config is never rewritten** — try `git config --global --get http.proxy` before and after; it is untouched. The plugin only adds flags to its own calls.
- **Off means "leave it alone", not "clear it".** With the switch off, no `-c` flags are added at all, so git falls back to whatever you configured globally (direct, or your own `git config` proxy). A `git p-on`-style global setting keeps working.
- **One Test button answers "is it the network or the repo?"** It probes the remote twice — once through the proxy and once direct — and reports both, so you can see at a glance which path is broken. If git isn't installed at all, the install dialog says so separately.
- **Credentials are treated as secrets.** A URL like `http://user:pass@host:port` has its password masked (`http://user:***@host:port`) everywhere it is sent to the browser, and is **omitted from exported bundles unless you tick "Include MCP secrets"**. The field echoes the masked form; saving it unchanged, or editing only the host/port, **keeps the stored

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：- Add, edit, delete and toggle `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` rows, and inspect servers declared elsewhere in config read-only.
- Shows live state per server: enabled/disabled, reconnection phase, and how many tools are currently registered.
- Secret handling: API tokens and headers are **never read back to the browser** — only key names. Editing preserves keys you didn't retype, and lets you delete individual keys explicitly.
- Type `${MY_TOKEN}` in any env or header value and it is written as a real `!!js` expression (`\`Bearer ${process.env.MY_TOKEN}\``) — DSH has no `${VAR}` interpolation, so this is the only mechanism that actually reads the environment. The `!!js` tag round-trips byte-exactly through every edit.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：**MCP servers that require OAuth**

Streamable-HTTP servers behind OAuth (Linear, Notion, Sentry and many hosted MCP endpoints) work too, even though DSH itself does not support it:

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：- **Why the plugin has to do it.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` builds its transport as `new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(url, { requestInit: { headers } })` — its config schema has only `url` and `headers`, **no `authProvider`**, and it never surfaces `UnauthorizedError`. So there is no hook to hand DSH an OAuth provider. The plugin runs the authorization-code flow itself and writes the resulting token into that row's `Authorization` header, which DSH then sends like any static bearer.
- **Standards-based, no secrets to register.** It discovers the protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728) and authorization-server metadata (RFC 8414 / OIDC), registers itself as a public client (RFC 7591), and uses **PKCE S256** with no client secret. `resource` is sent per RFC 8707 so the token is scoped to that server.
- **The browser does the login.** The callback listener binds **only `127.0.0.1`** on a random port, validates `state` with a constant-time compare, and shuts down as soon as the code arrives (5-minute timeout).
- **Tokens never reach the browser.** The UI sees only "authorized / expired", the expiry time, and whether a refresh token exists. `ref

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：**Backup: export / import your setup (for moving machines)**

The **Backup** tab packs everything this plugin manages — **Skills + MCP servers + Git source records** — into a single JSON file you can import on a new machine.

Two payload modes, chosen at export time:

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：| Mode | Contains | Size | On import |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Recipe** (default) | Just the source: repository + commit + layout | usually a few KB | Re-clones from the recorded repo — **needs network** |
| **Full contents** | The skill files too (binaries as base64) | can be several MB | Restores files directly — **works offline** |

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Features：- **Skills with no recoverable source always carry their contents**, in either mode — otherwise they would be lost on the new machine. That is not left to the UI to get wrong.
- **Import reviews before it writes**: the plan lists every entry's action (create / overwrite), conflicts, secrets that need re-entering, and blocked items. Nothing is written until you confirm.
- **Secrets are excluded by default.** This plugin normally never returns a secret to the browser; exporting breaks that boundary, so it takes an explicit opt-in and then shows a plain-text warning. Without it, only key names are written and you are told which ones to fill in.
- Import is **idempotent**: re-importing the same file overwrites rather than duplicating.
- If an upstream repository has moved on, the import reports that the commit it got differs from the one exported.

text: dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · How hot reload works：DSH has **no runtime API to add, remove, or restart an MCP connection**. A server is a loader row, and the supported way to change it is to edit its configuration and let HMR remount the row. This plugin writes to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, which DSH's HMR watches, then polls the loader to confirm the row actually remounted.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · How hot reload works：- **MCP enable/disable** sets the row's `disabled` boolean → HMR disposes or mounts the connection in place.
- **MCP add/edit** rewrites the row → HMR swaps in a fresh connection. Tool names stay stable across the swap.
- **Skill enable/disable** renames a file → the provider's watcher invalidates the catalog.

The panel reports what actually happened: when a change is written but the host has not finished remounting, it says so rather than claiming success.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Configuration isolation：MCP rows are written inside a dedicated managed block:

```yaml

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · >>> dsh-skill-mcp-tool:mcp:begin：- insert:
    - id: smt-mcp-<serverName>
      name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client"
      config: { ... }

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · <<< dsh-skill-mcp-tool:mcp:end：```

Everything outside the markers is preserved **byte for byte**, so other plugins' managed blocks (for example `dsh-skill-mcp-panel`) and your hand-written rows are never touched. Rows owned by other tools appear as read-only "external" servers. Writes take a `<file>.smt.lock` lock and use an atomic temp-file rename, so a concurrent writer cannot corrupt the file.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Plugin configuration：Optional `config` on the row in `cordis.patch.yml`:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dshHome` | `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh` | Harness home used to locate skill roots, the profile patch, and the source record |

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Files it touches：| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` | MCP server rows, inside the managed block |
| `<dshHome>/skills/**` | Skills it installs, creates, edits, or toggles |
| `<dshHome>/skill-mcp-tool/sources.json` | Index of Git install sources (an index only — deleting it never affects installed skills) |
| `<dshHome>/skill-mcp-tool/settings.json` | Plugin settings — currently just the Git proxy. Kept out of `cordis.patch.yml` on purpose: this plugin owns only the bytes between its MCP markers |
| `<dshHome>/skill-mcp-tool/update.json` | Progress of the last self-update (phase, exit code, from/to version). Written by the child process, so the panel can read it even after a restart |
| `<dshHome>/skill-mcp-tool/update.log` | Output of the last `pnpm add` run, shown in the panel on failure |
| `<dshHome>/skill-mcp-tool/oauth.json` | MCP OAuth records, including refresh tokens, mode 600. Tokens never reach the browser; only the access token is written into `cordis.patch.yml` |
dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · HTTP routes：All routes are same-origin, POST-only for writes, with an origin check that rejects cross-site requests.

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · HTTP routes：| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `state` | Skills + MCP + sources + proxy + environment in one read |
| `skill/set-enabled`, `skill/remove`, `skill/read`, `skill/write` | Skill management |
| `skill/install`, `skill/update`, `skill/check-updates`, `skill/forget-source` | Git sources |
| `mcp/list`, `mcp/save`, `mcp/remove`, `mcp/set-enabled` | MCP management |
| `mcp/oauth/status`, `mcp/oauth/authorize`, `mcp/oauth/refresh`, `mcp/oauth/forget` | OAuth for HTTP MCP servers: state / start authorization / rotate token / disconnect |
| `proxy/get`, `proxy/save`, `proxy/test` | Git proxy: read / write / probe both paths |
| `bundle/export`, `bundle/plan`, `bundle/import` | Settings export / review / import |
| `update/check`, `update/status`, `update/apply` | Self-update: compare with upstream / poll progress / start it |

dsh-skill-mcp-tool README · Plugin Info：| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| One-line value | Unified Skills + MCP manager with hot-reload toggles and Git-based skill install/update |
| Category | Skills & MCP |
| Supported profiles | desktop / web |
| Compatibility | DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x; Node.js ^22.15 or >=24; Windows / macOS / Linux |
| Permissions & services | Reads/writes the profile `cordis.patch.yml` and local skill roots; runs `git` for install/update (optionally through a proxy you configure); no telemetry |
